I confirm the reader's finding independently. All 10 blocks follow the rule: CN 17694913 LOT-k prints k for k = 1..37, every LOT_NUMBER matches exactly, the CANs have no lot sections, the numbers differ (no G1) and there is one lot-publishing notice (no G2). The fault is the shape, not the code: 7 blocks are single contracts for several lots, and each prints only one of those lots in LOT_NUMBER. 17821481 RES-1 says 'обособени позиции 5, 6, 15, 16' and is on LOT-5: 709,431.63 BGN against LOT-5's 189,067.00, close to the 4-lot sum of 720,590.02. RES-2 (28, 31) is on LOT-28: 14,294.96 against 552.00 (the 2-lot sum is 10,852.96). RES-5 (3, 8, 17) is on LOT-3: 445,146.37 against 55,671.10 (sum 427,375.45). RES-6 (21, 22, 23) is on LOT-21: 49,770.11 against 26,347.05 (sum 56,821.78). RES-7 (12, 18, 20, 25, 26, 27, 29, 30) is on LOT-12: 243,840.20 against 82,736.80 (sum 259,602.44). 17830774 RES-1 (33, 34, 35) prints the middle number, 34: 119,628.52, which is exactly the 3-lot sum. That shows LOT_NUMBER here is an arbitrary pick from the contract's lots. 17830774 RES-2 (1, 4, 14, 36) is on LOT-1: 186,058.74 against 74,213.08 (sum 127,185.18). Each winner is right for its printed lot. But the API now says that lot alone was awarded at the multi-lot value, and the text contradicts that. Before 568 these blocks stayed on the Tender, which was accurate. Three blocks are fine: RES-3 (position 24 only), RES-4 (no positions named; 13,733.10 against 13,884.20) and 17840150 RES-1 (position 2 only; 127,541.75 against 72,983.40, high but for one position). decision.md has no class for 'one block, several lots, one printed number', and step 9 bars the title evidence that exposes it. This is a gap in the rule, not a bug in the code.

items.why: The buyer's own corrigendum confirms the head. Version 3 of the tender is notice 18810459 (2016/S 108-192970, which references the award notice 2016/S 099-177443). Its TED-CONTENTS reads: 'Zamiast: II.2.1) Całkowita końcowa wartość zamówienia: Wartość: 6 351 557 614,20 PLN ... Powinno być: Wartość: 63 515 576,14 PLN, łącznie z VAT 8%'. In English: 'Instead of PLN 6,351,557,614.20, read PLN 63,515,576.14, including 8% VAT'. So the 6.35 bn was a x100 slip, and the head's new value of 6351557614 cents (PLN 63,515,576.14) matches the corrected figure to the cent. The figure is also consistent with the award notice. Notice 18771158 has 85 award blocks, and their TED-VALUE_COST values add up to exactly 6351557614 cents. That notice's procedure TED-VALUE is the slipped 635155761420. The contract notice 18696746 has 88 lots ('Pakiet nr 1..88') and no value fields, so no other total competes. All 85 blocks were checked against the head. Each block's LOT_NUMBER equals the contract-notice TED-LOT_NUMBER of the lot it sits on, and each awarded amount equals the block's VALUE_COST. This holds where the numbering shifts too, because pakiety 57, 63 and 81 have no award block: for example RES-57 prints 58 and sits on LOT-58 (Interferonum), RES-74 prints 76 and sits on LOT-76 (Trastuzumabum, PLN 9.08 M), and RES-85 prints 88 and sits on LOT-88 (Pembrolizumab). No number is printed twice. A total of PLN 63.5 M including VAT is plausible for one Gdańsk oncology hospital's drug and contrast-media supply; PLN 6.35 bn is not. One cosmetic point: amounts[] still lists the raw result_value 635155761420, but value_derivation.refused marks it as refused.
